event.title: Grupo Tan Tan
event.categories_json: [{"name":"live music","slug":"live-music","term_group":0,"term_taxonomy_id":26,"taxonomy":"tribe_events_cat","description":"","parent":0,"count":2706,"filter":"raw","id":26,"urls":{"self":"https://sanchosmx.com/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/categories/26","collection":"https://sanchosmx.com/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/categories"}}]
event.description:
Experience the roots of conjunto music in its purest form.

Grupo Tan Tan (AKA Los Callejeros) returns to Sanchos Cantina & Cocina for a series of shows highlighting the home grown sounds of classic conjunto music in the breeding grounds of a neighborhood cantina.

True to the origins of conjunto music Grupo Tan Tan will be playing classic conjunto songs as a trio with the use of accordion, bajosexto, and tololoche.

Song lists will include popular polkas, waltzes, huapangos, rancheras, and cumbias by trailblazers and founders of the conjunto genre like Flaco Jimenez, Tony de la Rosa, Nicky Snick Villarreal, Santiago Jimenez, and Steve Jordan.

The group will also dive into classic and contemporary norteño, county, oldies, and cumbias that formed the sounds native to San Antonio. These songs will include artists such as Grupo Frontera, Los Tigres de Norte, Vicente Fernandez, Los Tucanes, Ramon Ayala, Anecito Molina, and Johnny Cash.

This series of shows is the type of event that anyone who is a lover of culture should not miss and we encourage everyone to bring friends and family as we hope these type of events will help foster a growing appreciation for our unique San Antonio culture.

See you on the dance floor!

event.description:
Cooper’s Is Closed in observance of Memorial Day.

Closed on Memorial Day

As we take a moment to honor and remember the brave men and women who made the ultimate sacrifice while serving our country, we would like to inform you that we will be closed on Memorial Day, [specific date].

Memorial Day is a day of reflection and remembrance, a time to pay tribute to those who selflessly dedicated their lives to protect our freedom. It is a day to gather with loved ones, visit memorials, and participate in ceremonies that commemorate the sacrifices of our fallen heroes.

❤️ At Cooper’s Seafood House, we hold deep respect for the significance of Memorial Day. We believe it is important to observe this day with solemnity and gratitude. Therefore, our doors will be closed on this day to allow our staff and customers to participate in honoring the memory of our servicemen and servicewomen.

⏰ We will resume our regular business hours on [next business day]. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and appreciate your understanding as we join the nation in paying tribute to our fallen heroes.

On this Memorial Day, we encourage you to take a moment to reflect, express gratitude, and honor the memory of those who made the ultimate sacrifice. Let us come together as a community to remember their bravery, their courage, and their unwavering commitment to our country.

Memorial Day, originally called Decoration Day, is a day of remembrance for those who have died in service of the United States of America. Over two dozen cities and towns claim to be the birthplace of Memorial Day. While Waterloo N.Y. was officially declared the birthplace of Memorial Day by President Lyndon Johnson in May 1966, it’s difficult to prove conclusively the origins of the day.

Regardless of the exact date or location of its origins, one thing is clear – Memorial Day was borne out of the Civil War and a desire to honor our dead. It was officially proclaimed on 5 May 1868 by General John Logan, national commander of the Grand Army of the Republic, in his General Order No. 11. “The 30th of May, 1868, is designated for the purpose of strewing with flowers, or otherwise decorating the graves of comrades who died in defense of their country during the late rebellion, and whose bodies now lie in almost every city, village and hamlet churchyard in the land,” he proclaimed. The date of Decoration Day, as he called it, was chosen because it wasn’t the anniversary of any particular battle.

On the first Decoration Day, General James Garfield made a speech at Arlington National Cemetery, and 5,000 participants decorated the graves of the 20,000 Union and Confederate soldiers buried there.

The first state to officially recognize the holiday was New York in 1873. By 1890 it was recognized by all of the northern states. The South refused to acknowledge the day, honoring their dead on separate days until after World War I (when the holiday changed from honoring just those who died fighting in the Civil War to honoring Americans who died fighting in any war).

It is now observed in almost every state on the last Monday in May with Congressional passage of the National Holiday Act of 1971 (P.L. 90 – 363). This helped ensure a three day weekend for Federal holidays, though several southern states have an additional separate day for honoring the Confederate war dead: January 19th in Texas; April 26th in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, and Mississippi; May 10th in South Carolina; and June 3rd (Jefferson Davis’ birthday) in Louisiana and Tennessee.

🇺🇸🎆 Important Notice: Cooper’s Seafood House Closure on the 4th of July 🎇🇺🇸

📆 At Cooper’s Seafood House, we believe in celebrating our nation’s independence and honoring this special day with our loved ones. Therefore, we would like to inform you that our restaurant will be closed on the 4th of July, allowing our staff and customers to enjoy the festivities and spend quality time with their families and friends.

🎉 However, fear not! We will be back in full swing on the 5th of July, ready to serve you with our delicious seafood creations, refreshing drinks, and warm hospitality. Join us as we continue to provide unforgettable dining experiences and create lasting memories.

🔔 While we won’t be open on the 4th of July, we encourage you to embrace the spirit of the holiday by participating in local events, fireworks displays, and enjoying the company of your loved ones. Let’s come together to celebrate the values of freedom, unity, and the American spirit.

🍽️ When we reopen on the 5th of July, we look forward to welcoming you back to our vibrant restaurant and treating you to a culinary journey filled with flavors that embody the essence of coastal cuisine. Our dedicated team is excited to serve you with our signature dishes, handcrafted cocktails, and exceptional service.

📍 Cooper’s Seafood House – Scranton PA
⏰ Closure: 4th of July
🔓 Reopening: 5th of July
📞 For inquiries, call 570.346.6883
🌐 Visit our website coopers-seafood.com for more information and updates.

event.description:
Cooper’s Is Closed in observance of Memorial Day.

Closed on Memorial Day

As we take a moment to honor and remember the brave men and women who made the ultimate sacrifice while serving our country, we would like to inform you that we will be closed on Memorial Day, [specific date].

Memorial Day is a day of reflection and remembrance, a time to pay tribute to those who selflessly dedicated their lives to protect our freedom. It is a day to gather with loved ones, visit memorials, and participate in ceremonies that commemorate the sacrifices of our fallen heroes.

❤️ At Cooper’s Seafood House, we hold deep respect for the significance of Memorial Day. We believe it is important to observe this day with solemnity and gratitude. Therefore, our doors will be closed on this day to allow our staff and customers to participate in honoring the memory of our servicemen and servicewomen.

⏰ We will resume our regular business hours on [next business day]. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and appreciate your understanding as we join the nation in paying tribute to our fallen heroes.

On this Memorial Day, we encourage you to take a moment to reflect, express gratitude, and honor the memory of those who made the ultimate sacrifice. Let us come together as a community to remember their bravery, their courage, and their unwavering commitment to our country.

Memorial Day, originally called Decoration Day, is a day of remembrance for those who have died in service of the United States of America. Over two dozen cities and towns claim to be the birthplace of Memorial Day. While Waterloo N.Y. was officially declared the birthplace of Memorial Day by President Lyndon Johnson in May 1966, it’s difficult to prove conclusively the origins of the day.

Regardless of the exact date or location of its origins, one thing is clear – Memorial Day was borne out of the Civil War and a desire to honor our dead. It was officially proclaimed on 5 May 1868 by General John Logan, national commander of the Grand Army of the Republic, in his General Order No. 11. “The 30th of May, 1868, is designated for the purpose of strewing with flowers, or otherwise decorating the graves of comrades who died in defense of their country during the late rebellion, and whose bodies now lie in almost every city, village and hamlet churchyard in the land,” he proclaimed. The date of Decoration Day, as he called it, was chosen because it wasn’t the anniversary of any particular battle.

On the first Decoration Day, General James Garfield made a speech at Arlington National Cemetery, and 5,000 participants decorated the graves of the 20,000 Union and Confederate soldiers buried there.

The first state to officially recognize the holiday was New York in 1873. By 1890 it was recognized by all of the northern states. The South refused to acknowledge the day, honoring their dead on separate days until after World War I (when the holiday changed from honoring just those who died fighting in the Civil War to honoring Americans who died fighting in any war).

It is now observed in almost every state on the last Monday in May with Congressional passage of the National Holiday Act of 1971 (P.L. 90 – 363). This helped ensure a three day weekend for Federal holidays, though several southern states have an additional separate day for honoring the Confederate war dead: January 19th in Texas; April 26th in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, and Mississippi; May 10th in South Carolina; and June 3rd (Jefferson Davis’ birthday) in Louisiana and Tennessee.

event.title: Bo Johnson
event.description:
Stand-up comedian Bo Johnson (Comedy Central, Don't Tell Comedy) comes to Coalition Theater!

Bo Johnson is a comedian from Seattle, Washington. He can be found headlining clubs, breweries, and appropriately sized theaters across the United States and Canada. His stand up has been featured on Netflix is a Joke Radio, season two of Kevin Hart Presents: Hart of the City on Comedy Central, Don’t Tell Comedy Secret Sets (twice), Hulu, & LOL Live! at the prestigious Just For Laughs comedy festival in Montreal. He was a finalist in the 39th annual Seattle International Comedy Competition and is a regular at festivals including Bumbershoot, SF Sketchfest, the Double Down Comedy Experience sponsored by Zappos, Life is Beautiful in Las Vegas, Rifflandia in Victoria BC, Prizefest, and Big Pine Comedy Festival in Phoenix. Bo has opened for major acts including Marc Maron, Joe Dombrowski, Jessica Kirson, and David Nihill. With a growing online audience Bo’s jokes have been viewed millions of times online. Most recently he released his first full length special, “Two Sailboats” in 2025. Deadline included Bo in their Future of Funny list and regarding his special wrote, “For my money, Bo Johnson had one of the best debut specials in recent memory in Two Sailboats, a self-released hour culminating in a joke performed by his father…”

event.title: Richmond Famous with Leslie and The Dots
event.description:
Live comedy. True Stories. Completely unscripted.

Richmond Famous is the city’s premier storytelling and improv show, featuring an all-star cast of Coalition performers and your favorite Richmond celebrities. Each month we welcome a new Richmond-area citizen as our featured guest. The guests share true stories from their lives, which the cast use as inspiration to create a hilarious comedy show right before your eyes!

Joining us this month is Leslie Lilburn of Leslie and the Dots! Leslie is a Northside singer-songwriter who grew up in scenic Front Royal, VA and moved to Richmond in 2021. Leslie's musical fingerprint bears traces of a unique combination of inspirations, including the British Invasion and Country music of the 60's/70's. The result is an assortment of songs infused with joy, beauty, and heartbreak that would be at home in a Tarantino film score. He passes his time in a well-appointed garage studio, Murphy’s Pocket, with his band, The Dots.

Leslie and The Dots released their debut, self-titled album on March 19, 2026. You can catch them playing all around the Richmond area. Among other events, Leslie and The Dots have been featured in the Shockoe Sessions Live and Bellwether Garage concert series.

Cast: Josh Blubaugh, Jess Brooks, Chandler Brooks, Hannah Clark, Laurel George, Purnam Jantrania, Matt Micou, David Pijor, Katie Samuelsen, Kathryn Schmidt

event.title: The Saturday Matinee
event.description:
The Saturday Matinee is a monthly improv comedy show featuring your favorite local performers and comedy at a reasonable hour. Come catch a show before dinner and be home in your favorite PJs by bedtime!

Each Matinee features long form improv comedy from two ensembles: one preexisting Richmond improv team and one Team from a Hat, made up of a selection of improvisers chosen at random at the previous month’s show.

What is long form improv, you ask? Good question! It is theater that is entirely made up on the spot. To your eyes, it will feel like a short play or sketch show. You may even wonder, at times, if the performers are using ideas they came up with beforehand and practiced together. But trust us, none of it is pre-planned. Come witness the magic.

Show Time: 5:30 p.m.
Entry Fee: Pay What You Wish

October Team from a Hat Cast: Fig, Stephen Haselhorst, Wyatt Johnson, Adam Royster, Madeline Smith, Rogue Syrena, Shelby Ware, Alexandra Williams
October Team from a Hat Coach: Nate Shepherd

October Featured Team: Ryan Dondero & Friends!

Team from a Hat – Rules for Entry
· Are you an improviser who would like to be on next month’s Team from a Hat? Signing up is easy! All you have to do is come to the Saturday Matinee and throw your name in the Hat. At the end of the show, we will draw eight names to join forces and become next month’s Team from a Hat.
· To sign up for a Team from a Hat, you must have completed the basic improv curriculum at any comedy theater. For example, if you trained at Coalition, you must have completed the classes through level 401. No other experience is required.
· Each Team from a Hat is provided a dedicated coach for the month and will have three rehearsals together leading up to that month’s show. Rehearsals will be on Mondays at 7:00 to 9:00 p.m.
· Members of the current month’s Team from a Hat must wait one month (i.e., to the next show) to put their name back in the Hat.
· NOVEMBER INFO: The next show will be November 14. The coach will be Josh Wright. Team from a Hat rehearsals will be October 26, November 2, and November 9.

Questions about the show? Email nate@nateshepherd.com.

Producer: Nate Shepherd
Graphic Design: Eric Gordon
Art: Sterling Frost

Richmond Ballet presents Peter and the Wolf
featuring the Richmond Ballet Studio Company and Trainees

Peter and the Wolf
Choreography by Ma Cong
Music by Sergei Prokofiev
Narration by Daphne Maxwell Reid

Introduce the next generation to the joy of ballet with Peter and the Wolf, a beloved classic reimagined and expanded by Richmond Ballet Artistic Director Ma Cong. Follow Peter and his animal friends on a thrilling adventure to outsmart a mischievous wolf and discover that courage and teamwork can overcome even the greatest challenges. Unique to this production is a prologue filled with even more fairytale characters, including the Three Little Pigs and Little Red Riding Hood.

This family ballet, created for children and designed to appeal to audiences of all ages, is an engaging 45-minute performance that combines expressive choreography, narration, and moments of audience interaction. Featuring all-new costumes and sets by internationally acclaimed and award-winning designers, Peter and the Wolf offers a magical first ballet experience and a memorable adventure for the whole family.

Saturday, October 3 at 11am and 1pm
Sunday, October 4 at 11am and 1pm
at Richmond Ballet Studio Theatre

Tickets are $25 (including online convenience fee). Visit etix.com or call the Richmond Ballet Box Office at 804.344.0906 x224 open M-F from 11:00am-6:00pm. 

Peter and the Wolf is funded by the generosity of an anonymous donor

Artwork by Scenic Designer Emma Kingsbury

event.description:
Moving Art Two: Elevation

October 22-November 1, 2026  
at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts 

Moving Art Two: Elevation welcomes audiences into a world of contemporary ballet designed to stir the senses and elevate the unexpected.  

Ode
Choreography by Katarzyna Kozielska
Music by Various Artists 

Melodia
Choreography by Ma Cong
Music by Lhasa de Sela 

COLORFORMS
Choreography by Myles Thatcher
Music by Steve Reich 

Ode is a breathtaking exploration of kinetic energy, space, and human connection by Katarzyna Kozielska. A prominent voice in contemporary European ballet, Kozielska has created works for leading companies including Tulsa Ballet, Czech National Ballet, and Chemnitz Ballet. Shaped by her long career with Stuttgart Ballet both on and off the stage, Kozielska’s distinctive choreography unfolds through expansive movement and expressive lyricism. 

Artistic Director Ma Cong brings Melodia, an evocative work inspired by the music of acclaimed singer Lhasa de Sela, to Richmond Ballet. This 2007 creation harnesses the passion of the human voice to capture the profound beauty of shared experiences.

Classical technique meets a vibrant, modern landscape of shifting geometry in COLORFORMS by celebrated San Francisco Ballet soloist Myles Thatcher. This sought-after creator, whose work has been commissioned by renowned companies including New York City Ballet, Joffrey Ballet, and Scottish Ballet, transforms movement into a living work of art in this visually striking ballet.  

Dates & Times
Thursday, October 22 – 6:30 PM (Opening Night)
Friday, October 23 – 6:30 PM
Sunday, October 25 – 1:30 PM
Thursday, October 29 – 6:30 PM
Friday, October 30 – 6:30 PM
Sunday, November 1 – 1:30 PM 

Tickets start at $31*. Visit etix.com or call the Richmond Ballet Box Office at 804.344.0906 x224 open M-F from 11:00am-6:00pm.

Opening Night
Attend opening night of our Moving Art productions and receive exclusive access to a post show Q&A session and reception with guest choreographers and the professional dancers of Richmond Ballet. This is a unique opportunity to enjoy beer, wine, and hors d’oeuvres and mingle with our incredible team of artists. Opening night tickets, which start at $61*, reflect the added benefits.  

The cocktail hour at the post-show artist reception for Moving Art Two is sponsored by Dominion Energy. 

*this price includes facility and online convenience fees

event.description:
Moving Art Two: Elevation

October 22-November 1, 2026  
at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts 

Moving Art Two: Elevation welcomes audiences into a world of contemporary ballet designed to stir the senses and elevate the unexpected.  

Ode
Choreography by Katarzyna Kozielska
Music by Various Artists 

Melodia
Choreography by Ma Cong
Music by Lhasa de Sela 

COLORFORMS
Choreography by Myles Thatcher
Music by Steve Reich 

Ode is a breathtaking exploration of kinetic energy, space, and human connection by Katarzyna Kozielska. A prominent voice in contemporary European ballet, Kozielska has created works for leading companies including Tulsa Ballet, Czech National Ballet, and Chemnitz Ballet. Shaped by her long career with Stuttgart Ballet both on and off the stage, Kozielska’s distinctive choreography unfolds through expansive movement and expressive lyricism. 

Artistic Director Ma Cong brings Melodia, an evocative work inspired by the music of acclaimed singer Lhasa de Sela, to Richmond Ballet. This 2007 creation harnesses the passion of the human voice to capture the profound beauty of shared experiences.

Classical technique meets a vibrant, modern landscape of shifting geometry in COLORFORMS by celebrated San Francisco Ballet soloist Myles Thatcher. This sought-after creator, whose work has been commissioned by renowned companies including New York City Ballet, Joffrey Ballet, and Scottish Ballet, transforms movement into a living work of art in this visually striking ballet.  

Dates & Times
Thursday, October 22 – 6:30 PM (Opening Night)
Friday, October 23 – 6:30 PM
Sunday, October 25 – 1:30 PM
Thursday, October 29 – 6:30 PM
Friday, October 30 – 6:30 PM
Sunday, November 1 – 1:30 PM 

Tickets start at $31*. Visit etix.com or call the Richmond Ballet Box Office at 804.344.0906 x224 open M-F from 11:00am-6:00pm.

Opening Night
Attend opening night of our Moving Art productions and receive exclusive access to a post show Q&A session and reception with guest choreographers and the professional dancers of Richmond Ballet. This is a unique opportunity to enjoy beer, wine, and hors d’oeuvres and mingle with our incredible team of artists. Opening night tickets, which start at $61*, reflect the added benefits.  

The cocktail hour at the post-show artist reception for Moving Art Two is sponsored by Dominion Energy. 

*this price includes facility and online convenience fees

Sunday, December 6 – 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM

event.description:
The Nutcracker

December 5-23, 2026  
with Richmond Symphony at Dominion Energy Center

Choreography and Original Direction by Stoner Winslett
Music by Peter Ilyich Tchaikovsky

Step into a world of enchantment where holiday dreams come to life.  

Richmond Ballet’s beloved production of The Nutcracker returns to delight audiences of all ages with stunning choreography, lavish sets and costumes, and Tchaikovsky’s iconic score played live by the Richmond Symphony. Join Clara on her magical journey to the Kingdom of Sweets in this cherished annual tradition.  

Dates & Times
Saturday, December 5 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Sunday, December 6 – 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM
Friday, December 11 – 7:00 PM
Saturday, December 12 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Sunday, December 13 – 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM
Friday, December 18 – 7:00 PM
Saturday, December 19 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Sunday, December 20 – 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM
Monday, December 21 – 7:00 PM
Tuesday, December 22 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Wednesday, December 23 – 1:00 PM

Tickets start at $33.60*. Visit etix.com or call the Richmond Ballet Box Office at 804.344.0906 x224 open M-F from 11:00am-6:00pm.

*this price includes facility and online convenience fees 

The runtime for this performance is approximately 2 hours including one 20 minute intermission.

Please note: Strobe lighting and smoke effects are used in the production.

Richmond Ballet does not offer separate pricing for children. Each guest age 2 and up must have a ticket. Ticket prices are subject to change based on availability.

The Nutcracker

December 5-23, 2026  
with Richmond Symphony at Dominion Energy Center

Choreography and Original Direction by Stoner Winslett
Music by Peter Ilyich Tchaikovsky

Step into a world of enchantment where holiday dreams come to life.  

Richmond Ballet’s beloved production of The Nutcracker returns to delight audiences of all ages with stunning choreography, lavish sets and costumes, and Tchaikovsky’s iconic score played live by the Richmond Symphony. Join Clara on her magical journey to the Kingdom of Sweets in this cherished annual tradition.  

Dates & Times
Saturday, December 5 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Sunday, December 6 – 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM
Friday, December 11 – 7:00 PM
Saturday, December 12 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Sunday, December 13 – 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM
Friday, December 18 – 7:00 PM
Saturday, December 19 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Sunday, December 20 – 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM
Monday, December 21 – 7:00 PM
Tuesday, December 22 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Wednesday, December 23 – 1:00 PM

Tickets start at $33.60*. Visit etix.com or call the Richmond Ballet Box Office at 804.344.0906 x224 open M-F from 11:00am-6:00pm.

*this price includes facility and online convenience fees 

The runtime for this performance is approximately 2 hours including one 20 minute intermission.

Please note: Strobe lighting and smoke effects are used in the production.

Richmond Ballet does not offer separate pricing for children. Each guest age 2 and up must have a ticket. Ticket prices are subject to change based on availability.

Tchaikovsky: The Man Behind the Music

February 12-14, 2027 
with Richmond Symphony at Dominion Energy Center  

Choreography by Ma Cong
Music by Peter Ilyich Tchaikovsky 
Additional music by Alexander Glazunov, Mikhail Glinka and Fritz Kreisler 

Behind one of the world’s most legendary composers lies a soul, a secret, and a story waiting to be told.  

Tchaikovsky: The Man Behind the Music is a sweeping full-length ballet by Ma Cong that explores the life and artistry of Peter Ilyich Tchaikovsky and the relationships that shaped him. With powerful choreography and profound emotional depth, this production reveals the tension between Tchaikovsky’s public success and private turmoil, providing a rare glimpse into the heart of ballet’s most renowned composer.   

Dates & Times
Friday, February 12 – 7:00 PM
Saturday, February 13 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Sunday, February 14 – 2:00 PM

Moving Art Four: Director’s Choice

May 13-23, 2027 
at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts  

Refined elegance and raw power take the stage in Moving Art Four: Director’s Choice.  

The Leaves are Fading
Choreography by Antony Tudor
Music by Antonín Dvořák 

Gnawa
Choreography by Nacho Duato
Music by Various Artists 

The Leaves are Fading is a reflection on memory, love, and the passage of time set to the lush music of Antonín Dvořák. The elegant choreography of Antony Tudor — a pioneering British choreographer who revolutionized 20th century ballet — weaves together fleeting moments of romance in this poignant masterwork.  

Featuring the rich music of North Africa and the Mediterranean, Gnawa pulses with rhythmic energy and spiritual intensity. Spanish visionary and global icon Nacho Duato blends athletic contemporary movement with earthy sensuality to create a mesmerizing work that celebrates the universal power of music and dance.

Moving Art Four: Director’s Choice

May 13-23, 2027 
at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts  

Refined elegance and raw power take the stage in Moving Art Four: Director’s Choice.  

The Leaves are Fading
Choreography by Antony Tudor
Music by Antonín Dvořák 

Gnawa
Choreography by Nacho Duato
Music by Various Artists 

The Leaves are Fading is a reflection on memory, love, and the passage of time set to the lush music of Antonín Dvořák. The elegant choreography of Antony Tudor — a pioneering British choreographer who revolutionized 20th century ballet — weaves together fleeting moments of romance in this poignant masterwork.  

Featuring the rich music of North Africa and the Mediterranean, Gnawa pulses with rhythmic energy and spiritual intensity. Spanish visionary and global icon Nacho Duato blends athletic contemporary movement with earthy sensuality to create a mesmerizing work that celebrates the universal power of music and dance.
